instructions: Pour both cans of chickpeas into a medium saucepan, liquid and all. Set it over medium heat and warm the chickpeas for 5 minutes, until they're hot.
Meanwhile, mince the 2 garlic cloves. Put them in a medium bowl with 1/4 tsp of the salt and press and scrape them with the flat of the knife until they turn into a paste.
Juice the lemon. That should be about 3 tbsp. Add it to the bowl with the 5 tbsp tahini, the 1/2 tsp cumin and 3 tbsp of the olive oil, and whisk. It will look thick and clumpy for now.
Ladle 1/4 cup of the hot chickpea liquid into a cup and set it aside. Turn off the heat and drain the chickpeas in a sieve.

Add the drained chickpeas to the bowl along with the 1/4 cup liquid and the other 1/4 tsp salt. Press about half the chickpeas against the side of the bowl with a fork so they break, and leave the rest whole. Stir until the tahini turns creamy and coats everything.
Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Slice the cucumber and tomatoes, and chop 1/4 cup of the parsley.
Transfer the chickpeas to a wide shallow bowl and spread them out. Drizzle the remaining 3 tbsp olive oil over the top and scatter on the parsley.
Serve with the sliced cucumber and tomatoes.
method_notes: Zaatar and Zaytoun is the lead: canned chickpeas warmed in their own liquid, then crushed lightly into a tahini, lemon and garlic sauce with cumin, finished with olive oil, so it's ready in minutes. Curious Cuisiniere and Beach House Kitchen make it with dried chickpeas and add chilli or a longer cook, and Beach House Kitchen serves it with a chopped salad; all three agree the chickpeas stay mostly whole in a loose tahini sauce. The lead serves it with flatbread, which is left out here to keep it gluten-free, so the vegetables and parsley do the serving. No version had 20 or more ratings (the lead shows 5 from 1 vote) and RecipeTin Eats has no msabaha, so Zaatar and Zaytoun leads as the closest quick Lebanese version.
